What we wire, install and maintain

From the main switchboard to the last camera, one team handles the full electrical scope.

Power distribution

Cable containment

Trays and ladders that keep power and data runs tidy, safe and easy to service.

Industrial installations

CCTV and security

Solar and battery storage

Inverters and batteries installed safely, with isolators and protection in place.

Control and AV racks

Neat rack builds and wiring for control rooms, conference and sound systems.

Structured cabling

Dressed, labelled data cabling for offices, server rooms and plants.

Network and security racks

Patch panels, switches, power backup and alarm panels mounted and cabled cleanly.

Work we take pride in

From the blog

Practical notes from our team on safe, tidy and fairly priced electrical work.

Safety firstOctober 2026

Why tidy cabling is safer cabling

Neat cable runs do more than look good. They make faults easier to find and keep heat and strain under control.

Read more

Crowded, tangled bundles trap heat, hide damaged insulation and turn a ten-minute fix into a long outage. Separating power from data, supporting cables on trays, and labelling both ends of every run keeps the installation safe and quick to service.

It also protects your budget: a well-documented installation costs less to extend or repair years later.

Cost honestOctober 2026

What an honest electrical quote should include

A good quote lets you compare like for like and leaves no room for surprises on the final bill.

Read more
  • Materials and labour listed separately
  • The rating and type of key components
  • What is not included in the price
  • A realistic start date and finish date
  • Testing and handover documents
  • How changes to the scope will be priced
PlanningOctober 2026

Before you add solar: five quick checks

A little preparation up front keeps a solar and battery installation safe, on schedule and on budget.

Read more
  • Review your monthly electricity use
  • Check roof space and shading
  • Have the distribution board and earthing inspected
  • Decide where isolators and the inverter will sit
  • Plan safe access for future maintenance
